raw_response.overlap_rationale: Both papers are readable full-text articles published by Nandita Singh in Volume 10 of Gender, Technology and Development (2006) drawing on the same SIDA-funded rural Indian water ethnographic research programme, with Study B's entire 27-village sample nested inside Study A's 32-village sample. Specifically, Study B analyzes 12 villages in two districts of Madhya Pradesh (Datia and Shivpuri) and 15 villages in three districts of West Bengal (2002-2004 fieldwork), including 12 focus group discussions (five women-only). Study A analyzes those exact same 12 villages in two districts of Madhya Pradesh and 15 villages in three districts of West Bengal—plus 3 villages in one district of Bihar and 2 villages in one district of Jharkhand (32 villages total; 162 women and 149 men; the exact same 12 FGDs including five women-only). Furthermore, both papers report identical empirical findings from the overlapping Madhya Pradesh/West Bengal fieldwork, including the exact 30% female attendance rate across 12 village Panchayats, two village PRI handpump siting cases where SC women were excluded by upper-caste siting (named Lamkana and Saprar in Study B), and women's nominal membership in NGO-led arsenic removal plant committees in West Bengal, while Study A additionally reports handpump rejection and 15 TRYSEM-trained women mechanics across MP, Bihar, and Jharkhand.
raw_response.study_a_sample_and_data: Ethnographic fieldwork across 32 rural Indian villages in four states: 12 villages in 2 districts of Madhya Pradesh (including Shivpuri), 15 villages in 3 districts of West Bengal, 3 villages in 1 district of Bihar, and 2 villages in 1 district of Jharkhand (SIDA-funded project). Sample comprises 162 women and 149 men (N = 311 informants) via participant observation, key-informant interviews, 12 focus group discussions (5 women-only), 4 village case studies, 55 handpumps in 17 villages (MP, Bihar, Jharkhand), 15 women trained as handpump mechanics under TRYSEM, and 12 village Panchayats in MP.
raw_response.study_b_sample_and_data: Ethnographic fieldwork conducted between 2002 and 2004 across 27 rural Indian villages in two states: 12 villages in 2 districts of Madhya Pradesh (Datia and Shivpuri; examining PRI Women and Child Welfare and Health Committees and 12 village Panchayats, including villages Lamkana and Saprar) and 15 villages in 3 districts of West Bengal (examining NGO-initiated community arsenic removal plant committees, including village Raipara), using participant observation, interviews, and 12 focus group discussions (5 women-only).
